title: Multi-tool detection: shadow-bridged tools merge into one blob
description: Reported by user: a photo of 5 pocket knives laid side by side on the template (public/samples/five-knives.jpg) is detected as a single merged blob instead of 5 separate tools. Root cause: the knives are close enough that cast shadow bridges adjacent tools, and for several knife pairs the shadow is not meaningfully lighter than the (often black) knife material itself, so no single global or per-pixel-local intensity rule separates them by tool identity. Confirmed empirically: a fixed-threshold sweep from 20-150 (in outline.ts's segment()) never produces 5 non-overlapping, tall-narrow (knife-shaped) blobs — low thresholds produce wide horizontal fragments that all span nearly the full row width, high thresholds merge everything into one blob. An Otsu+adaptiveThreshold AND-combination was also tried (with a fill-enclosed-holes step to avoid gutting solid-color tools) and passed all synthetic/manual-mode tests, but on the real photo it produced 5 blobs with plausible total area yet wrong shape (each ~130mm wide x 30-46mm tall horizontal bands, i.e. illumination-gradient artifacts, not per-knife silhouettes) — this was caught only by checking aspect ratio/shape, not by the existing tests (which only assert blobs.length > 0 and log area). That approach was reverted; do not re-attempt pure global/local-intensity segmentation on this fixture without a new idea — it has been ruled out.
design: Two viable directions identified, not yet chosen: (1) A manual 'split' UI gesture — user drags a line across a merged blob's outline to cut it into two polygons; deterministic, composes with the existing vertex editor (OutlineEditor), ships value immediately regardless of photo quality. Pair with a capture-guidance hint (space tools >= ~10mm apart, shoot with even/overhead lighting) since the top of this photo's knife row, where shadow was weakest, already separated into distinct runs at some thresholds. (2) Further segmentation research using non-intensity signals (e.g. color/hue where knives differ from the shadow, or an edge/gradient-based approach) — higher effort, uncertain payoff, not attempted this session.
acceptance_criteria: Given public/samples/five-knives.jpg, detectBlobs (or a new UI-assisted flow) yields 5 blobs, each with an x-range that does not overlap any other's by more than ~3mm, and each roughly knife-shaped (height:width aspect ratio >= ~4:1, width in the 20-35mm range). Any automated test added for this must check shape (aspect ratio / bbox), not just blob count or area, since area-only checks passed on the wrong (banded) result during investigation.

title: Fix dev-mode memory blow-up from ImageData props
description: React 19.2 dev-mode Components profiler diffs old/new props recursively (addObjectDiffToProperties), enumerating up to 3 levels deep. Viewer/StepPanel receive raw ImageData (rectified.image, outline.mask, photo.image) as props, causing tens of millions of enumerated entries per render, heap jumping from 84MB to 2.2GB, and a DataCloneError OOM crash under npm run dev. Fix: wrap large buffers in an opaque Box<T> class (private field, nothing enumerable) before passing as props.
close_reason: Wrapped ImageData/large-polygon props (photo, rectified, outline, exportResult, effectivePolygon) in src/lib/box.ts's opaque Box<T> before passing to Viewer/StepPanel, keeping React 19.2 dev profiler's prop-diff enumeration off the pixel buffers.
